speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: While many countries have also embarked on a drive to attract global talent, others have turned increasingly inward and there are indications that such sentiments are growing in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: This is natural, because at its basic, global talent policies are about allowing people into our home.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: It is therefore not only a practical matter but also an emotive one.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: As such, a winning global talent strategy must rely not only on facts and figures; it must also build comfort and give assurances to our local Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Global talent policies look at attracting and retaining global talent in Singapore that is complementary to our local workforce.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: But a global talent strategy is far more complex because it must take into consideration many other areas that are intrinsically intertwined, including education, upskilling and reskilling, national identity and culture, economic development and competitiveness, entrepreneurship, research, housing, law enforcement amongst others.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Over the past few months, the hon Minister for Manpower has, in great detail and quite painstakingly set out how the various global talent schemes work, including new schemes like OnePass and COMPASS.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: He has also explained the rationale for adjustments that have been made to existing schemes.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: And I am in agreement with the Minister that these are steps in the right direction.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: In fact, today, the Minister and I have also agreed on the colour scheme for our outfit, and it is purely incidental, Mr Speaker.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: These programmes have, in part, led to Singapore being consistently recognised as one of the top countries in the world for global talent to consider moving to.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: So, overall, we are recognised internationally as doing very well and we can take heart that our global talent policies are generally sound.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: In my Adjournment Motion today I will look at areas ancillary but related to our global talent policies and that must form part of our global talent strategy.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Areas that will ultimately affect their success because they tug at the hearts of Singaporeans; they affect our fears, our hopes and aspirations, our dignity and our way of life; and they will largely determine whether we support these policies.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: I will make some suggestions on how the Government can bolster our global talent policy, ameliorate local concerns and get more of our people behind these policies that are a key plank to ensure Singapore’s continued competitiveness and prosperity.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Most Singaporeans are realistic in recognising that we cannot indigenously produce all the talent required to fuel and grow our economy.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: As an advanced economy, many of the higher-skilled jobs require not just a first-class education, but often also specific skills and international experience.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: This is what our global talent policies seek to fill.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Singaporeans are, in my view, comfortable if these roles are filled on the basis of a utilitarian impermanence.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Unfortunately, for some reason, there appears to be an impression that our global talent policies are synonymous with immigration.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The Government has been quite clear that these policies and our open arms are in our self-interest.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The initial impetus should not be about immigration bolstering our population numbers or immediately settling in as residents.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The first impetus is to fill gaps in our economy.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: This transactional first instance will be a testing phase, to see if they like us and we like them.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: If it is a match, then we should certainly invite them to become Permanent Residents and citizens.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: This is because as much as we say that we are ourselves a nation of immigrants, over our decades of independence, we have formed an identity of our own and become a proud nation and a proud people.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Hence, we must ensure that foreigners seeking to settle here respect and accept our national identity, shared values and our way of life.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: If this meeting of minds and hearts are amongst the chief considerations and criteria for residency and citizenship, it will ameliorate the concerns of Singaporeans that naturalised citizens and permanent residents are going to be foreign from us, or even worse, that they will all be fabulously rich, beyond our understanding, and more "atas" than us.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: It will also render irrelevant any distinction sought to be made between Singapore-born Singaporeans and naturalised Singaporeans – a distinction some quarters have sought to make.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: My view is that emphasising a transactional initial relationship with global talent will not affect Singapore’s attractiveness as a magnet for global talent.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: In Dubai, for example, it is near impossible to become a citizen and yet, it has not had any trouble attracting a cosmopolitan pool of global talent to set up shop there, with many staying for the long term.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Changes were made to their citizenship rules last year, but the criteria remain extremely stringent and even under the new rules, citizenship will only be offered to a very exceptional few.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Immigration and our global talent policy, although related, should not be seen as one and the same.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: I therefore encourage the government to emphasise that citizenship and to a certain extent, permanent residency is not merely a matter of skills and qualifications, but also one of fit and acceptance.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: This could be done by, for example, elaborating on how ICA assesses the criteria of whether a person would be able integrate into our society or whether they are ready to set roots down in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: ICA could also consider publishing examples of how such criteria could be met, which aside from providing transparency to locals, has the added benefit of allowing potential applicants to know what it takes to become a Singapore Citizen.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: I now come to my next point, Sir, on respect.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Whether on a work pass or a permanent resident, global talent coming to Singapore are our guests and we, as Singaporeans, are their hosts.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: As much as we are hospitable and welcoming, it is also perfectly reasonable to expect that our global talents here respect their hosts.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: I suggest three key “respects” that global talent should keep in mind when coming here.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The first "respect" is respecting our laws and regulations.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Singaporeans get particularly inflamed when we see incidents of foreigners flouting laws.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: This is because we, as a people, are famously law abiding and we expect others to be the same in our country.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: A case in point was the public furore that arose over foreigners gathering outside bars and restaurants in May 2020, which was during the circuit breaker when such gatherings were disallowed.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Although incidents like this have nothing to do with a global talent policies, commentators are always very quick to ask what they are employed as in Singapore and what are the consequences of them flouting the law.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: These flashpoints often lead to a backlash against our global talent policies.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Tellingly, in relation to this particular incident, MOM had to respond to queries related to work passes, saying in a statement, that "foreigners working in Singapore must abide by our laws and that those convicted, regardless of the type of work pass they hold risk having them revoked and banned from working in Singapore".

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The second "respect" is respect for our culture, sensitivities and ways of doing things.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Expatriates in Singapore should seek, as far as possible, to learn how we do things and to adapt.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: This is one of the aims of the National Integration Council (NIC).

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: I have looked at some of the resources provided by the NIC on its website and there are many suggestions as to how Singaporeans can reach out to expatriates and make them feel comfortable here.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Expatriates must also abide by our ways of doing things.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: These may be small things like respecting personal space or simple courtesies which are the norms here but may not be expected behaviour in their home countries.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Over time, if there are expats or expat communities who ignore these norms, certain opinions and biases may be formed against them.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: These are difficult things to talk about because we do not want to generalise; but these are hard conversations we must have.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Clearly, more effort needs to be made on both sides to ease our expatriate friends into Singapore’s culture.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The third “respect” is respect for the capabilities of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: We need to make it a culture to consider locals first, in particular, for expats coming in who are in decision making or influential roles affecting hiring.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: We expend massive resources to educate, train, retrain our people and we have become one of the most highly skilled workforces in the world.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: It is also one of our competitive advantages to attract investment.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: We must not allow our local workers to be overlooked due to preferences other than merit.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The curriculum and guidelines for such a programme could be produced by the NIC.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Bringing global talent into Singapore must also have a knock off effect on the skills and competencies of our own people and our own companies.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: As I mentioned earlier, we should look to adopt an initial transactional approach to global talents coming in to fill jobs.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Our foreign workforce must shift and it must mould itself around us.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: And this is what I believe is MOM’s new schemes and adjustments will be able to achieve.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: However, it is not possible for this replacement to follow the course of an exact science.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: It is not possible to pick a foreigner and say, "Well I have someone local to replace you.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: This replacement will instead, be dynamic and will be aided precisely by COMPASS, the FCF and dependency ratios.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Some global talent, we should not be too quick to replace: entrepreneurs, researchers, inventors and rainmakers because they have a timeless quality and they are enablers.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: By their very nature, they will not replace Singaporeans, but they will create opportunities for us.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: This replacement is, however, also dependent on us grooming our local talent to themselves become global talent.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: It is not being a foreigner that makes one a global talent, it is the fact that these people have worked in other countries, some in many other countries and that they have international experience and networks.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Such exposure is invaluable and in order for our local talent to become global talent, we must encourage the acquisition of precisely this quality.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Our local Universities are recognised as some of the very best in the world and this has led to some comments that since we have the best universities, why do we need global talent to come into Singapore.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: It is naïve to believe that one can graduate from our local University, work locally and then be able to take up top spots in MNCs.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: In Singapore, if one does not have international exposure, it will be increasingly difficult to compete for these top spots.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: As a global hub, we attract multinational corporations that look at the world as its talent pool because they want to get in the global best.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: My suggestion is that we need to do more not only at the universities but even at the Secondary level to encourage a global mindset amongst our local students who are our future workers.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: This should not only be in our school curricula or in the form of exchanges with other schools, but also through attachments with global companies and their laboratories, factories and facilities overseas or even in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: In particular, we need to build a strong group of future workers who are well-acquainted and well-connected with Southeast Asia and APAC.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: This is especially important because of the growing number of corporate regional headquarters being set up in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The Singapore worker must see herself as a global worker – either working overseas for a time or travelling for work if based in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: These are the roles that we must be prepared for.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: For Singaporeans who gain experience overseas, after some time, we look forward to welcoming them back home to take up senior positions here.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: And we have exemplars, in fact, even in this House, our very own hon Nominated Member Janet Ang is one such person who has worked overseas for many years and then returned to Singapore to head an MNC.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Let us endeavour to produce more Janet Angs.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Michael came to Singapore in 2007 and he worked in various companies before co-founding Kabam in 2020.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Kabam builds next generation robotic and connectivity solutions for built-environment businesses.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Despite being a pandemic baby, has seen rapid growth over its two years of operations, partnering and providing services to, amongst others, Certis, the Singapore Land Authority, Singapore Technologies and Konica Minolta.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Michael acts as the CEO of Kabam and his co-founders Kelvin Wee and Benjamin Chia credit him, with his prior experience in bomb disposal, subsea vehicles and logistics robotics, with the company’s rapid growth.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The criteria they apply to whom they seek to hire must also be very strict, to ensure that they thoroughly consider local applicants before looking at foreign candidates.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Again, control mechanisms like the salary stipulations for each type of pass, dependency ratios, the FCF and COMPASS, will operate to as far as possible, make sure that locals are considered first in SMEs before foreign talent may be admitted.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: In fact, if we look at the various policies that govern how we approach global talent, it is quite clear that the criteria for a foreigner to come to work in Singapore is very stringent and that the system is heavily weighted towards Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: In fact, as much as there has been suggestions that foreigners are taking jobs from Singaporeans, many local businesses have asked instead that the regime be loosened to make it easier for skilled foreigners to come into Singapore.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: On the practical side, the Government must calibrate policies to take into account shifts in the global talent market and our own local talent pool becoming more skilled and globally exposed and it does appear that MOM is doing this.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: And because we know that this is such an emotive topic, even us, Members of this House, politicians and public figures must also be careful not to seek to politicise the issue for political gain or publicity.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: It does Singapore no good for us to be seen as xenophobic or anti-foreigner.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: I am optimistic, Sir, for Singapore’s continued success as a global city and an international hub.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: I look forward to a more cosmopolitan business environment, fuelled by our hardworking and skilled local workforce, tapping on international expertise, building Asia’s capital city and the world’s hub for commerce, business exchanges, ideas and global talent.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As the Member shared, globally, our efforts have not gone unrecognised.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I agree with the Member that it is important to get more support for these policies because they are a key gateway or bridge to ensure our beloved Singapore’s continued competitiveness and prosperity.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Rob Khoo is currently Head of Marketing, Communications and Sustainability at EDPR Sunseap, which is a solar energy company.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: His entrepreneurship journey shows how Singapore’s openness has brought about more opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Opportunities not just to MNCs, but also to local startups.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Not just to companies, but also to individuals.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Colleagues from countries such as the US, Canada, Australia, Hong Kong and China taught him critical technical and people management skills.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: When he subsequently decided to pivot to renewable energy and started his own solar panel company, his overseas colleagues and partners from Australia and Europe taught him everything he needed to know about the technology.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: With the Overseas Networks and Expertise (ONE) Pass bringing in more top talent, more MNCs, more SMEs and Singaporeans will benefit.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This is especially as ONE Pass holders will be able to take on multiple roles which gives them the opportunity to nurture local startups, even as they are employed elsewhere.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The future of Singapore is dependent on successfully bringing in talents as well as developing local talents.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: It is crucial for these talents to be able to come together, to integrate well and to work together.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To this end, the Member has raised two key suggestions.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As the Member has shared, we maintain a clear distinction between our work pass and immigration framework.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Work pass holders can put in applications and a select group is able to obtain PR, based on a holistic assessment of the factors that I have just elaborated earlier on.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: While we do not provide any guarantee or fast tracks to PR for our EP and ONE Pass holders, we hope that, as they spend time in Singapore, top talent will choose to make Singapore their home.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Granting PR or Citizenship to deserving global talent means that we can anchor them here to continue creating opportunities for Singapore and Singaporeans in the long run.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: There are clear benefits if work pass holders are well-integrated into Singapore's society.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: A healthy respect for our laws, our culture and their local colleagues will make for less friction in the workplace and, at the same time, produce stronger teams.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As the Member suggested, we can also help them ease into their stay here through orientation programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Currently, senior EP holders are engaged by tripartite partners when they first come to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Started in July 2021, these engagements are part of the broader efforts under the National Integration Council (NIC) to promote workplace integration.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: During these in-depth, small group engagements, we share Singapore's approach to key workforce and workplace issues, including maintaining fair and harmonious labour relations and ensuring good local-foreign integration in companies.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We want to seek to strike a balance between promoting integration and not being overly prescriptive in how we achieve this aim.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Employers also have an important part to play in supporting foreign employees who are new to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For instance, DBS Bank launched their own Singapore Immersion Programme.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: It assigns all new employees a Singaporean buddy and it organises activities, such as sharing sessions on Singapore's nation-building journey and walking trails exploring our multi-cultural heritage.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Companies interested in implementing similar ground-up integration initiatives can tap on the Community Integration Fund (CIF), which is administered by MCCY.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As the Member also pointed out, we expect all employers, regardless whether they are local or foreign, to fairly consider local candidates for available jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Our intent is to create a level playing field for locals.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We provide the necessary tools, at every step of the way, for locals to strengthen their own capabilities – we invest in education, from preschool to tertiary education; we have programmes that locals can tap on to upskill, reskill and make career transitions; and we provide financial support for those who may have been hurt or hit by curve balls in life.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We cannot guarantee the same outcomes for everyone.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In the near future, we will expand the range of actions that we can take through the workplace fairness legislation.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Second, developing a global mindset amongst our future workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As the Member has shared, gaining overseas exposure is key to taking up leadership positions later, especially in global companies.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have programmes to start such capability building early.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: MOE works with Institutes of Higher Learning on initiatives for students, such as overseas internships and educational exchanges.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will further nuance it by working with MOE colleagues to see how we can start cultivating the global mindset even earlier.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: However, developing a global mindset is not something that the Singapore Government can do alone.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: It requires our workforce, our individuals, to be willing to learn, to be ambitious to have the hunger to succeed and to be tenacious to overcome challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: It also requires companies to devote resources to nurturing young local talents.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will do more with unions, workers and companies.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We encourage everyone to participate in our Forward Singapore engagement sessions and to contribute ideas.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: By being open to the world, we have benefited from global best practices.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have created new opportunities and we have uplifted livelihoods.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Looking forward, Singapore must continue to remain open to the world, to prepare for the next phase of growth.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We must remain open to global talent who can bring even more opportunities to our shores.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: And as Singaporeans, for us, we must prepare our current workforce to continue to take advantage and leverage these opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Government will continue to work hand in hand with unions, workers and our companies to build a vibrant, thriving global city that will be brimming with opportunities for all of our fellow Singaporeans.
